strings.d1.s0.name: Osaka Castle
strings.d1.s0.tips: Toyotomi's castle: views from the 8th floor, a quiet park in the morning, cherry blossom in April.
strings.d1.s1.name: Osaka Castle Park
strings.d1.s1.tips: Parkland and moats around the castle, plus a plum grove.
strings.d1.s2.name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
strings.d1.s2.tips: Osaka's kitchen: tuna from the stall, wagyu skewers and strawberries, all eaten standing up.
strings.d1.s3.name: Shinsaibashi-suji
strings.d1.s3.tips: A 600 m covered arcade with Don Quijote and drugstores and cosmetics.
strings.d1.s4.name: Dotonbori
strings.d1.s4.tips: The Glico running man and neon lights; try takoyaki (Wanaka) and Mizuno okonomiyaki, with crowds all along the canal.
strings.d1.b0.name: Mizuno Okonomiyaki
strings.d1.b0.tips: A Bib Gourmand okonomiyaki (savoury pancake) in Dotonbori, made with a yam batter.
strings.d1.b1.name: Tombori River Cruise
strings.d1.b1.tips: A 20-minute canal boat ride past the neon.
strings.d2.s0.name: Shitennoji Temple
strings.d2.s0.tips: Japan's oldest Buddhist temple (593), with a pagoda and garden.
strings.d2.s1.name: Shinsekai
strings.d2.s1.tips: A retro entertainment district with Tsutenkaku Tower and the Billiken statue.
strings.d2.s2.name: Tsutenkaku Tower
strings.d2.s2.tips: A tower from 1912 with an observation deck and a slide.
strings.d2.s3.name: Kushikatsu Daruma Shinsekai
strings.d2.s3.tips: Deep-fried skewers; double-dipping in the sauce is forbidden.
strings.d2.s4.name: Abeno Harukas 300
strings.d2.s4.tips: The observation deck of Japan's tallest building, with views over Osaka and the sea.
strings.d2.b0.name: Yakko Kushikatsu
strings.d2.b0.tips: If Daruma is full, it is on the same street.
strings.d2.b1.name: Tennoji Park & Zoo
strings.d2.b1.tips: A park and zoo, as an alternative to Harukas.
strings.d3.s0.name: Nara Park
strings.d3.s0.tips: 40 minutes from Osaka by Kintetsu; 1,200 free-roaming deer, crackers 200 JPY, quiet in the morning.
strings.d3.s1.name: Todai-ji
strings.d3.s1.tips: A 15 m Buddha inside the world's largest wooden building; crawl through the hole in the pillar.
strings.d3.s2.name: Kasuga Taisha
strings.d3.s2.tips: A Shinto shrine with 3,000 stone lanterns, reached by a forest path.
strings.d3.s3.name: Nakatanidou Mochi
strings.d3.s3.tips: A show of high-speed mochi pounding; try the fresh yomogi (mugwort) mochi.
strings.d3.s4.name: Naramachi
strings.d3.s4.tips: A district of old merchant houses with cafés and crafts, Nara's quiet side.
strings.d3.b0.name: Kamameshi Shizuka Nara
strings.d3.b0.tips: Rice cooked in an iron pot; a hot lunch.
strings.d3.b1.name: Kofuku-ji
strings.d3.b1.tips: A five-storey pagoda, as an alternative to Naramachi.
strings.d4.s0.name: Umeda Sky Building
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Floating Garden Observatory: clear in the morning, among the best views in Kansai.
strings.d4.s1.name: Nakanoshima Park
strings.d4.s1.tips: A park on an island between two rivers, with a rose garden and the city hall.
strings.d4.s2.name: Osaka Nakanoshima Museum of Art
strings.d4.s2.tips: A museum in a black cube, with Modigliani and Osaka art.
strings.d4.s3.name: Tenma Kisaburo
strings.d4.s3.tips: A local restaurant in Tenma serving a daily teishoku (set meal).
strings.d4.s4.name: Tenjinbashisuji Shopping Street
strings.d4.s4.tips: Japan's longest covered shopping street (2.6 km), full of local shops.
strings.d4.b0.name: Hanshin Department Store Snack Park
strings.d4.b0.tips: A standing-room food floor in Umeda; try ikayaki (grilled squid).
strings.d4.b1.name: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living
strings.d4.b1.tips: A re-created Edo-period street, with kimono rental.
strings.d5.s0.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
strings.d5.s0.tips: 45 minutes from Osaka by JR; 10,000 red torii gates, empty at 07:30, so climb halfway up the mountain.
strings.d5.s1.name: Kiyomizu-dera
strings.d5.s1.tips: A temple with a wooden terrace, views over Kyoto and the streets of Higashiyama.
strings.d5.s2.name: Nishiki Market
strings.d5.s2.tips: Kyoto's kitchen: tsukemono (pickles) and tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), eaten standing up.
strings.d5.s3.name: Gion
strings.d5.s3.tips: The geisha district, with Hanamikoji Street and Yasaka Shrine.
strings.d5.s4.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
strings.d5.s4.tips: A bamboo tunnel; the crowds thin out in the late afternoon. Cross Togetsukyo Bridge.
strings.d5.b0.name: Kyoto Gogyo Ramen
strings.d5.b1.name: Kinkaku-ji
strings.d5.b1.tips: The Golden Pavilion, as an alternative to Arashiyama.
strings.d6.s0.name: Universal Studios Japan
strings.d6.s0.tips: Super Nintendo World (area tickets run out in the morning) and Harry Potter; 1-Day Pass about 8,900 JPY, Express Pass is worth it in crowds, queue before the 08:30 opening.
strings.d6.s1.name: Universal CityWalk Osaka
strings.d6.s1.tips: Restaurants by the park exit, plus a takoyaki museum.
strings.d6.s2.name: Tempozan Ferris Wheel
strings.d6.s2.tips: A Ferris wheel on Osaka Bay with night lights, 10 minutes from USJ.
strings.d6.b0.name: Kaiyukan Aquarium
strings.d6.b0.tips: An aquarium with a whale shark, as an alternative to USJ.
strings.d6.b1.name: Osaka Bay Okonomiyaki Chibo
strings.d7.theme: Namba morning and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Namba Yasaka Shrine
strings.d7.s0.tips: A shrine with a stage shaped like a giant lion's head; good for photos.
strings.d7.s1.name: Hozenji Yokocho
strings.d7.s1.tips: Pour water over the moss-covered Fudo statue; a stone-paved lane.
strings.d7.s2.name: Wanaka Takoyaki Sennichimae
strings.d7.s2.tips: Osaka's classic takoyaki for a farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Namba Parks
strings.d7.s3.tips: A canyon-shaped mall with a rooftop garden; Kansai Airport is 40 minutes away by Nankai.
strings.d7.b0.name: Ichiran Namba
strings.d7.b0.tips: Ramen, as an alternative to takoyaki.
strings.d7.b1.name: Kuromon Ichiba Morning Tour
strings.d7.b1.tips: The market at its morning best; good for souvenirs.
strings.note0: An ICOCA card works on all trains. Kansai Airport is 40 minutes away on the Nankai Rapi:t. Nara and Kyoto are 45 minutes by Kintetsu or JR.
strings.note1: November brings momiji (autumn leaves) in Kyoto and April brings cherry blossom. Winter is dry at 5-10°C and uncrowded, and it is kani (crab) season.
strings.note2: Osaka is all about kuidaore (eat until you drop): takoyaki, okonomiyaki and kushikatsu cost 500-1,500 JPY. Go to Kuromon in the morning.
strings.note3: For the USJ Nintendo area, book an area ticket in the app when the park opens. Express Pass costs 10,000+ JPY.
strings.note4: Cash still matters; use the 7-Eleven ATMs. There is no tipping, and people queue quietly.
strings.note5: Fushimi Inari is empty at 07:30; tour buses arrive after 09:00.
strings.transit.name: ICOCA
strings.transit.why_chosen: It works on the Osaka Metro, JR and Hankyu, and uses the same system as Suica.
